notes: Short summary: BlueQuill is a mid-stage media tech platform using LLMs for customer support & content indexing.
Primary ask: predictable throughput for high-concurrency chat during scheduled drops (marketing-driven).
Quote (CTO): "We need 99th percentile chat latency under 120ms at steady-state; peaks can tolerate higher tail but want graceful degradation."
Traffic shape: steady daytime QPS ~85, peak burst QPS ~950 (20x spikes for 10-15 minute windows).
Payloads: average 600 tokens/request, peaks up to 4k tokens for long-context summarization flows.
Cost sensitivity: medium — prepared to commit to reserved capacity if SLA and predictable unit economics are clear.
Routing needs: multi-region with failover, ability to route lower-priority traffic to quantized variants during peaks.
Security: require VPC private deployment, customer-managed KMS, audit logs forwarded to SIEM, 18 month retention on request.
workshop_goals: Validate baseline QPS and token/sec assumptions with traffic traces.
Model mapping: which model families to reserve vs use as fallbacks (quantized 8-bit for background tasks).
Define SLA targets: p50/p95/p99 latency targets, allowed tail increases during bursts.
Estimate GPU reserve: initial recommended pool = 12 A100-equivalent GPUs for target latency at 95th percentile with autoscale buffer.
Cost runbook: tradeoffs between batching, KV-cache TTL, and prefix caching to reduce token throughput.
POC acceptance criteria: sustained 95th percentile latency <150ms at 1-hour simulated launch traffic with fallbacks in place.
